title: Impact of the Middle East Situation on Singapore
what_it_is: Impact of the Middle East Situation on Singapore

sections.label: Ministerial Statements on Parliamentary Questions
sections.summary: Ministerial Statements will address Parliamentary Questions Nos 1 to 62 and written Nos 1 to 12, with political officeholders responding on their areas.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Our Ministerial Statements will address Parliamentary Question Nos 1 to 62 in today's Order Paper, as well as written Parliamentary Question Nos 1 to 12, and related Parliamentary Questions (PQs) filed for subsequent Sittings.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: And as this is a whole-of-Government approach, may I also seek your permission to allow relevant political officeholders to respond to clarifications pertaining to their respective areas of responsibilities?

sections.label: Vessels through Strait of Hormuz
sections.summary: Last month about six vessels a day passed through the Strait of Hormuz, compared to around 135 normally.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Last month, only about six vessels on average passed through the Strait of Hormuz each day, compared to around 135 in normal times.

sections.label: Brent crude and LNG prices
sections.summary: Since the conflict began, Brent crude doubled from US$71 to US$141 per barrel and spot LNG doubled from US$11 to US$22 per MMBtu.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Since the onset of the conflict, Brent crude oil prices have doubled from US$71 per barrel just before the conflict, to a peak of US$141.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Similarly, spot liquefied natural gas (LNG) prices have also doubled, from US$11 per million British Thermal Units (MMBtu) to as high as US$22/MMBtu.

sections.label: MTI monitoring and GDP forecast
sections.summary: MTI will continue to monitor developments closely and will update its GDP forecast in May.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: MTI will continue to monitor developments closely and will update our GDP forecast in May.

sections.label: Regulated electricity tariff increase
sections.summary: The regulated electricity tariff most Singapore households pay rose 2.1% to about 27.27 cents per kWh for 2026's second quarter.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: The regulated electricity tariff, which most Singapore households pay, increased by 2.1% to about 27.27 cents per kilowatt hour (kWh) for the second quarter of 2026.

sections.label: Fuel costs and electricity prices
sections.summary: Fuel is about half the tariff, so higher fuel prices will flow through, and a sharper increase is expected in the next tariff adjustment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Fuel makes up about half of the tariff, so higher fuel prices will flow through to electricity prices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: We should therefore expect a much sharper increase in the next tariff adjustment, which will fully reflect the higher costs of fuel.

sections.label: Higher 2026 inflation projection
sections.summary: Singapore's overall inflation for 2026 is now expected to be higher than earlier projected.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Consequently, we now expect Singapore's overall inflation for 2026 to be higher than earlier projected.

sections.label: MAS inflation outlook assessment date
sections.summary: MAS will consider these developments in its upcoming inflation outlook assessment, to be released on 14 April 2026.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: MAS will take these developments into account in its upcoming assessment of the inflation outlook, which it will release on 14 April 2026.

sections.label: Energy conservation and economic resilience
sections.summary: Households and businesses can conserve energy, and Singapore must press on with Economic Strategy Review recommendations to stay resilient and competitive.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Households can do our best to conserve electricity, use climate vouchers to purchase more energy efficient appliances and adopt simple measures, such as using fans instead of air-conditioning and taking public transport instead of driving.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Businesses can also conserve energy by tapping on schemes, such as the Energy Efficiency Grant, and investing in more efficient equipment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Periods of disruption, such as this, will test the resilience of countries and economies, but they also create impetus for firms to transform, diversify and deepen their capabilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: We must press on with the recommendations of the Economic Strategy Review – including building global leadership in key growth sectors, such as advanced manufacturing and modern services, supporting firms to diversify and internationalise, and accelerating enterprise transformation through technology and innovation, so that our economy remains resilient and competitive in a more challenging global environment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: If we stay disciplined, deepen our trust in each other, preserve our capabilities and use this period to sharpen our competitive edge, Singapore will be well placed not only to weather this crisis, but to emerge from it stronger.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister for Finance, and the Coordinating Minister for National Security and Minister for Home Affairs, will also be making related Ministerial Statements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: I will allow Members to raise points of clarifications on all Statements after Minister Shanmugam's Statement.

sections.label: Largest Budget on record
sections.summary: On 12 February 2026, the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance presented the largest Budget on record, at $155 billion.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: On 12 February 2026, the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance presented our largest Budget on record, at $155 billion.

sections.label: Cash payout for drivers
sections.summary: The Government will disburse $200 in cash to active platform workers, private hire car drivers and taxi drivers from the end of the month.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: To provide further relief, the Government will disburse $200 in cash to active platform workers, private hire car drivers and taxi drivers from the end of the month.

sections.label: Enhanced Corporate Income Tax rebate
sections.summary: The Corporate Income Tax rebate announced at Budget will be enhanced from 40% to 50% for the Year of Assessment 2026 to help businesses manage cashflow.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: To help businesses manage cashflow, we will enhance the Corporate Income Tax rebate announced at Budget from 40% to 50% for the Year of Assessment 2026.

sections.label: Energy efficiency grant expansion
sections.summary: The grant's base tier is expanded to all sectors and extended to 31 March 2028 so more companies can invest in energy-efficient equipment.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: Companies in these sectors can make use of the Grant to invest in new, energy-efficient equipment.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: We will now expand the base tier of this grant to all sectors and extend this support for another year, to 31 March 2028, so that more companies can benefit.

sections.label: Cost-of-living support brought forward
sections.summary: CDC vouchers are brought forward to June 2026 and the Budget 2026 Cost-of-Living Special Payment is raised by $200 for eligible Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: But we know the situation has amplified cost of living anxieties for Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: Therefore, to reassure Singaporeans that the cost increases in the impending months can be managed, we will bring forward the disbursement of the $500 CDC vouchers announced in Budget this year from January 2027 to June 2026.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: We will also increase the Budget 2026 Cost-of-Living Special Payment by $200 for all eligible Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: About 2.4 million Singaporeans will receive this additional payment in cash, which will be disbursed in September.

sections.label: Additional measures package total
sections.summary: The package adds up to close to $1 billion in additional measures on top of Budget 2026 commitments, with drawer plans available.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: We have drawer plans, and as events develop, we can put them into action and do more if the situation calls for it.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: This package adds up to close to $1 billion in additional measures, on top of what has previously been committed in Budget 2026.

sections.label: Homefront Crisis Executive Group role
sections.summary: The HCEG coordinates across Government agencies to anticipate emergencies, prepare contingency plans and respond to homefront crises; the HCMC was formalised after SARS in 2003.

sentences.speaker: The Coordinating Minister for National Security and Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: At the Civil Service level, there is the Homefront Crisis Executive Group (HCEG).

sentences.speaker: The Coordinating Minister for National Security and Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: The HCEG coordinates across Government agencies, to anticipate potential emergency scenarios, ensure the necessary contingency plans are prepared and respond to the impact of any homefront crisis or emergency.

sentences.speaker: The Coordinating Minister for National Security and Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: The HCMC is a structure that was formalised after the Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome (SARS) outbreak in 2003.

sections.label: Prime Minister orders HCMC stand-up
sections.summary: The Prime Minister asked that the HCMC be stood up some weeks ago to deal with the current crisis.

sentences.speaker: The Coordinating Minister for National Security and Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: The Prime Minister asked that the HCMC be stood up some weeks ago to deal with the current crisis.

sections.label: Crude oil and gas imports
sections.summary: More than half of total crude oil imports come from the Middle East, and about 9% of natural gas would have been imported from Qatar before the crisis.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: More than half of our total crude oil imports comes from the Middle East.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Prior to the crisis, about 9% of our natural gas would have been imported from Qatar, if it had carried on as per normal through the year.

sections.label: Brent crude price surge
sections.summary: Brent crude has surged as high as 70% since hostilities increased on 28 February.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Brent crude has surged as high as 70% since the increase in hostilities on 28 February.

sections.label: GasCo buying replacement gas
sections.summary: GasCo has begun buying replacement natural gas to replace disrupted supply from Qatar.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: GasCo has begun buying replacement natural gas to replace the disrupted supply from Qatar.

sections.label: EMA electricity retailer requirements
sections.summary: EMA strengthened regulatory requirements on electricity retailers in 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Fourth, EMA has strengthened regulatory requirements on electricity retailers in 2023.

sections.label: Domestic solar energy deployment progress
sections.summary: The 2030 target of two gigawatt-peak was achieved in 2025, and the Government announced raising it to three gigawatt-peak.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: We have made good progress on domestic solar energy deployment.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: We have already achieved our 2030 target of two gigawatt-peak in 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: At the Committee of Supply debate in March, the Government announced that it would raise the target to three gigawatt-peak.

sections.label: Non-disclosure policy
sections.summary: As a policy, these are not disclosed.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: As a policy, we do not disclose these.

sections.label: Fuel and diesel duty question
sections.summary: Several Members asked if the Government will consider reducing fuel or diesel duties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: What I meant to say was that several Members have asked if the Government will consider reducing fuel or diesel duties.

sections.label: Food resilience and seafood supply
sections.summary: The Government is asked for its view on food resilience, given concerns that diesel shortages for regional fishermen may affect seafood and fish supply.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Second, can the Government share its view on food resilience, especially with some concerns about seafood and fish supply, with the risk that diesel shortages for fishermen in the region may affect supply?

sections.label: Inflation pass-through into 2027-2028
sections.summary: The question asks how likely inflation pass-through is to continue into 2027 and 2028 and whether further off-Budget measures are needed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: My question is, our macro policy mix to address this supply shock is very clear, but what is the likelihood of the inflation pass-through continuing into 2027 and even into 2028, and if there is a need for off-Budget measures where further tranches are needed?

sections.label: Maintaining strong Singapore dollar policy
sections.summary: The speaker says MAS will release its policy statement in April and stresses maintaining the strong Singapore dollar policy to control inflation pass-through.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: That has always been the case, but I think going forward, I am aware that MAS will be releasing its policy statement in April later on.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: But I think it is very important for us to continue to maintain our strong Singapore dollar policy to control inflation pass-through.

sections.label: Electricity from natural gas
sections.summary: The passage states that 95% of Singapore's electricity comes from natural gas.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: As everyone knows, 95% of our electricity comes from natural gas.

sections.label: Diversified LNG supplies via GasCo
sections.summary: Through GasCo, Singapore can source LNG worldwide and has diversified its LNG supplies beyond the Middle East.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: So, this has come in quite presciently, so that today, we are able to, through GasCo, source for supplies of LNG from all over the world.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: We have now diversified our LNG supplies beyond the Middle East.

sections.label: Quarterly audits of gencos
sections.summary: Quarterly audits of gencos check that advanced combined cycle gas turbines can switch to diesel, with audit statistics showing 99.9% readiness.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: We have conducted regular audits every quarter on these gencos to ensure that the advanced combined cycle gas turbine can switch to diesel.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Thus far, our audit statistics have shown that we are 99.9% ready in switching.

sections.label: LNG supply from Australia
sections.summary: The Prime Minister issued a joint statement with Australia's Prime Minister Albanese to establish ties and secure LNG supply from Australia.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: The key in point, as the Deputy Prime Minister shared, our Prime Minister has also issued a joint statement with the Prime Minister of Australia, Prime Minister Albanese, to establish ties and to ensure that we can continue to get supply of LNG from Australia.

sections.label: Renewable energy imports and subsea cables
sections.summary: About 8.35 gigawatts of renewable energy got conditional approval, exceeding the six gigawatt target, and negotiations are ramped up on feasibility studies and subsea cables.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Those conversations happen contemporaneously with our discussions on renewable energy imports.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: And to that end, if the Member recall, we have already awarded both conditional approval or conditional licensing of up to about 8.35 gigawatts of renewable energy.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Our original target was six gigawatts – we have exceeded that.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Today, given this uncertainty, we are indeed ramping up the negotiations, the discussions with our counterparts to see how we can expedite both the completion of the feasibility studies as well as the commercial feasibility of laying of the subsea cables.

sections.label: No first-of-a-kind technology adoption
sections.summary: Singapore will never put its population at risk by adopting first-of-a-kind technology, though it can be a fast adopter.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: And the Member will appreciate the fact that regardless of how we collaborate with the rest of the ASEAN member states, we will never put our population at risk of adopting a first-of-a-kind technology.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: We can be a fast adopter, but we cannot be the first-of-a-kind mover.

sections.label: Diesel prices and Iran tensions
sections.summary: Diesel prices rose mainly due to global factors, with ongoing tensions involving Iran increasing uncertainty and risk to oil supply.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Our diesel prices have risen mainly due to global factors.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: I mean the ongoing tensions involving Iran, as I have said a few times already, significantly increase the uncertainty and, of course, the risk to oil supply.

sections.label: Diesel demand and government action
sections.summary: Emphasis on diesel in agrarian countries explains its faster rise than petrol, and MTI will watch the space and the Government may act if needed.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: So, you can appreciate that because of the versatility and in farm tractors in many of the agrarian countries around, that emphasis has always been on diesel.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: That is why it has risen faster compared to petrol.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: MTI will continue to keep a close watch on this space and if need be, the Government will not hesitate to come in, to act, to help.

sections.label: Government and business pricing
sections.summary: The Government does not dictate business prices or price changes so long as prices are set independently.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: The Government does not dictate the prices or price changes of businesses, so long as the prices are set independently.

sections.label: Pump price competition monitoring
sections.summary: No evidence suggests the market structure is not competitive, and the Competition and Consumer Commission of Singapore will keep watching pump prices for anti-competitive behaviour.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: At present, there is no evidence to suggest that the market structure is not competitive.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: The Competition and Consumer Commission of Singapore will continue to watch closely the pump prices to make sure there is no anti-competitive behaviour by the businesses.

sections.label: Bus companies diesel cost increases
sections.summary: Local bus transport companies are badly affected by surging diesel prices, with some facing diesel cost increases of more than $1 million per month.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: Supplementary question two: the local bus transport companies are badly affected by the surge in diesel prices, and they are running diesel cost increases of more than $1 million per month for some of them.

sections.label: Capping pump prices distorts market
sections.summary: Regulating or capping petrol or diesel pump prices will distort the market and benefit vehicle users who consume more and possibly the more well-to-do.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: First, in the context of a petrol, which I mentioned earlier on, regulating or capping petrol or diesel pump prices will distort the market and actually will serve to benefit vehicle users and owners that consume more, and possibly people who are more well-to-do.

sections.label: Electricity prices and aviation fuel supply
sections.summary: The Government will continue to watch electricity prices closely, and is working with aviation stakeholders to monitor fuel supply, with no significant shortages now.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: On electricity prices, on whether it is a price threshold, the electricity prices is something that the Government will continue to watch closely because it affects households and businesses directly.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
sentences.text: We are working with the aviation stakeholders to monitor the fuel supply for aviation hubs carefully to ensure that it remains stable.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
sentences.text: There are no significant supply shortages for now as we have adequate fuel supply from the diversified sources.

sections.label: Middle East food import share
sections.summary: The Middle East accounts for less than 1% of Singapore's total food imports.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: The Middle East accounts for less than 1% of our total food imports.

sections.label: Fertiliser costs and food prices
sections.summary: No near-term food supply disruption is expected, but fertiliser costs have risen due to the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, impacting food prices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: (In Malay):   With regards to food, we do not expect a risk of food supply disruptions in the near term for Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: However, there is an impact today on fertilisers because fertiliser is a by-product of oil and supply has been affected due to the closure of the Strait of Hormuz.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Therefore, fertiliser costs have increased, and this will impact food prices.

sections.label: Strait of Hormuz LNG impact
sections.summary: The Strait of Hormuz affects about 9% to 10% of LNG supplies from Qatar, while a Red Sea blockade would mainly impact supplies from Europe via the Suez Canal.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: On the Strait of Hormuz, it impacts about 9% to 10% of our LNG supplies from Qatar.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: We think that a simultaneous choke or blockade of the Red Sea near the Gulf of Aden, where the Houthis from South Yemen – which is also something that I did highlight in my Facebook posts about a week ago – would not have a significant impact, because it primarily impacts supplies coming from Europe through the Suez Canal.

sections.label: Electricity tariff increase warning
sections.summary: The impact has not come into the regulated electricity tariff, but the next quarter's tariff will see significantly sharper increases.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: That is why that has not actually come into impact for the regulated tariff for electricity.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: I have also given everyone a warning that the next quarter's tariff will see significantly sharper increases.

sections.label: EV scheme for heavy vehicles
sections.summary: A $40,000 grant announced in March last year supports Singapore's EV scheme for heavy vehicles and funds chargers, the chief constraint on adoption.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: I just want to take the opportunity to do a plug for the Singapore's EV scheme for heavy vehicles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: We have a grant of $40,000, which we announced, I think in March last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: The scheme also covers the provision of funding for chargers, which actually is the chief constraint behind why the adoption of electric heavy vehicles is not as prevalent as say, passenger vehicles.

sections.label: Tariff increase cannot be held
sections.summary: The 2.1% increase in tariffs for this quarter cannot be held, and everyone must collectively take note.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: It is something that all of us collectively will have to take note of.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: We should not expect that for the 2.1% increase in tariffs for this quarter, I am able to hold it.

sections.label: Qatar and Shell force majeure
sections.summary: Qatar invoked force majeure due to the Strait of Hormuz, Shell invoked it on one or two cargoes, and GasCo secured replacement cargo at higher pricing.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Because of the Strait of Hormuz, Qatar has invoked force majeure.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: I think on one or two of the cargoes, Shell has also invoked force majeure.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: So, for us, for the GasCo, we have to make sure that we can get the replacement cargo.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: We have been successful in getting the replacement cargo.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: It is just that we are not able to get it at the earlier pricing.

sections.label: Trade in Essential Supplies agreement
sections.summary: The expansion will cover food resilience and food supply, and negotiations on the Agreement on Trade in Essential Supplies have been substantively concluded.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: At the same time, we will expand that to food resilience and food supply.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: We have substantively concluded the negotiations on the Agreement on Trade in Essential Supplies.

sections.label: Stockpile provisions and space constraints
sections.summary: The HCMC and HCEG are studying how to increase stockpile provisions, with space as the real constraint.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: As Coordinating Minister for National Security stated, the HCMC together with the HCEG are currently not resting on our laurels.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: We are studying how to increase the current stockpile provisions.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Our very real constraint is the space we have here.

sections.label: Scenario planning for chokepoints
sections.summary: There are different contingency and scenario plans for single-country and multi-country chokepoints.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: For the scenario planning, as I have shared with Prof Koh earlier on, we have different contingency, different scenario planning, for single-country chokepoints to multi-country chokepoints.

sections.label: Aviation fuel supply and SAF levy
sections.summary: Fuel supply is adequate though tanker arrivals may decline; the sustainable aviation fuel levy starts 1 January 2027 for contracts from October 2026.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: While the pragmatic pause responds to current geopolitical volatility, how is the Ministry working with our SAFCo to secure a long-term fixed-price sustainable aviation fuel supply contracts that might insulate our aviation hub's decarbonisation timeline from fossil fuel price spikes and regional instabilities?

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: There are no significant fuel supply shortages, and we have adequate fuel and bunker supply.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: We expect, however, tanker arrivals may decline the coming months, given the disruption to global energy flows.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: In relation to sustainable aviation fuel, at this point in time, it is a bit too early to disclose what our strategies would be.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: We have made the announcement that the sustainable aviation fuel levy would kick in come 1 January 2027 for contracts entered from October 2026 onwards at this point in time.

sections.label: Refinery compromise and cavern space
sections.summary: There will be some compromise in refinery capabilities and percentage loss with two fuel types needing cavern space to rebalance sour and sweet crude.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: So, what we have done is that there will be some compromise in the refinery capabilities.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: There is some percentage loss when you have one predominant fuel, to now, at least two different fuel types, because you then need the space, the caverns, for you to rebalance between sour and sweet crude.

sections.label: Support for Combi and limousine drivers
sections.summary: In 2002 the Government worked closely with NTUC on support measures for Combi bus and limousine drivers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: On self-employed groups, specifically the Combi bus and limousine drivers, in 2002, the Government worked very closely with the NTUC to work out the support measures for this particular group.

sections.label: Government co-paying large ticket items
sections.summary: The Government can consider co-paying for large ticket items through better financing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: In terms of large ticket items, and whether the Government can co-pay through better financing, that is something we can consider.

sections.label: Pre-approved energy-saving equipment support
sections.summary: Pre-approval aims to get support to companies quickly, based on work with trade and business associations on frequently used, energy-saving equipment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: Similarly, for pre-approved, the reason why it is pre-approved is because we want to make sure that we get the support to the companies as soon as possible, which is why we have worked very closely with trade associations and business associations to understand which are the types of equipment that businesses use most frequently and are most energy saving.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: And we are happy to take in inputs together with the applications.

sections.label: Straits of Hormuz energy shortages
sections.summary: The Straits of Hormuz blockade has caused global energy supply shortages, including crude oil and gas, and will impact essential products like raw materials.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs and Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: The Straits of Hormuz blockade has resulted in global energy supply shortages, including crude oil and gas, and will impact other essential products, such as raw materials.

sections.label: Support measures for businesses and individuals
sections.summary: Jeffrey Siow detailed support: enhanced corporate income tax rebates, expanded Energy Efficiency Grant, earlier CDC vouchers and an additional $200 Cost-of-Living Special Payment.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs and Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Acting Minister Jeffrey Siow has provided details on the support that will be given.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs and Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: We will launch immediate assistance to businesses through enhanced corporate income tax rebates and expand the Energy Efficiency Grant to all sectors.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs and Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: For individuals, we will issue CDC vouchers earlier and provide an additional $200 via the Cost-of-Living Special Payment from Budget 2026 for eligible Singaporeans to ease daily expenses.

sections.label: Thresholds for extending fuel measures
sections.summary: With diesel prices up to 70% higher, the question asks what thresholds will determine extension of similar measures for Singaporeans relying on vehicles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: Given the elevated prices of fuel, specifically diesel, now by up to 70%, what thresholds will determine the extension of similar measures today, to assist Singaporeans who rely on vehicles for their livelihoods?

sections.label: Targeted support for SMEs and drivers
sections.summary: Support is directed to SMEs, companies and drivers affected by fuel prices, through the Corporate Income Tax rebate and $200 for taxi and private hire car drivers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: And so, what we want to do is be more focused and targeted in who we support, and our approach therefore is to provide directed support to SMEs, companies, drivers – people who are more directly affected by the fuel prices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: And the overall package provides that support – whether it is through the Corporate Income Tax rebate, as I mentioned earlier, as well as other targeted support, like the $200, that we are giving to the taxi drivers, the platform workers, which includes the private hire car drivers.

sections.label: Review of financial assistance quantum
sections.summary: The question asks if MSF will review financial assistance quantum; the $200 was sized to the $150 to $250 average monthly fuel cost increase for full-time drivers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: I would therefore ask whether MSF would review the quantum of financial assistance provided to mitigate the expected sharp rise in food inflation in the next few months?

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: We sized the $200 based on the average increase in fuel cost that full-time taxi drivers as well as full-time private hire car drivers experienced in a month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: The average is about $150 to $250, so we have chosen a number that is in the middle of that range.

sections.label: Support for affected drivers
sections.summary: NTUC and the Land Transport Authority have discussed support with platform operators, which gave fuel vouchers to affected drivers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: In addition, we also note that NTUC as well as the Land Transport Authority, have been in discussions with the platform operators to provide support for these drivers and platform operators have given fuel vouchers in the last few weeks to the drivers that are affected.

sections.label: ComCare assistance rates revised
sections.summary: ComCare Short-to-Medium-Term Assistance rates were revised about a year ago, in April 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
sentences.text: In terms of the overall ComCare, be it the Short-to-Medium-Term Assistance rates, we have revised the assistance rates about a year ago, in April 2025.

sections.label: ComLink+ support enhancements announced
sections.summary: Enhancements to ComLink+ support were announced earlier during the Committee of Supply debates.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
sentences.text: In addition to that, earlier during the Committee of Supply debates, we also announced enhancements to ComLink+ support.

sections.label: Watching cost of living impact
sections.summary: Lower-income families are disproportionately affected by cost of living increases, and the situation is being watched closely for response in future tranches.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
sentences.text: Having said so, I just want to say we are cognisant that our lower-income families are affected by cost of living increases disproportionately.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
sentences.text: And therefore, we are watching the situation very closely and will be ready to respond should there be a need to in the next few tranches.

sections.label: Energy Efficient Grant expansion
sections.summary: Businesses should accelerate their shift to energy efficient equipment, and the Energy Efficient Grant is expanded to all sectors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Second, many businesses should make use of this time to accelerate their shift to energy efficient equipment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I am glad to hear that the Energy Efficient Grant is expanded to all sectors, and this is the right direction.

sections.label: Supporting SMEs through tax rebates
sections.summary: Support reaches SMEs fastest through Corporate Income Tax rebates and cash grants, with disbursement starting from April.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: It is important, therefore, for us to get support to the SMEs as soon as possible.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: And that is the reason why we have decided, the best way and the fastest way to get support to them is through the Corporate Income Tax rebates and through the cash grant, to provide them support in terms of cashflow considerations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: And we are able to disburse and start doing that from April onwards, which should help, even in those cases that the Member mentioned about the contracts being locked in at fixed prices.

sections.label: Transport affordability support for families
sections.summary: A comprehensive system supports lower-income Singaporeans' transport needs, with subsidies for large families using private hire vehicles, as fuel prices rose.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: Specifically, on her question on transport affordability especially for families, we do have a comprehensive system to support lower-income Singaporeans, in terms of their transport needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: It is, I believe, about 2% of the average household income for the P30, if I am not mistaken.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: Even for large families who need to take private hire vehicles, we have additional subsidies that we have worked in through the Large Family LifeSG Credits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: First, if we look at the fuel prices, petrol prices have gone up by 20% and diesel 70%.

sections.label: Cash run and fuel costs
sections.summary: The cash run component increased to about $2,000, an increase of $500, while monthly fuel cost for one diesel van rose $172.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: And if you look at the cash run component, it has been increased to about $2,000, basically an increase of $500.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: But some estimates have it that just the monthly fuel cost increase for one diesel van alone is already $172 a month.

sections.label: Medical supplies through Strait of Hormuz
sections.summary: Medical supplies through the Strait of Hormuz are below 1% of medical supplies, which are about 12% of total healthcare costs, so impact is not significant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Our medical supplies that come through the Strait of Hormuz are very low, well below 1% of our medical supplies, and medical supplies in turn, is about 12% of our total healthcare costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: So, the impact is not significant and there is no tap on our stockpiles.

sections.label: Enabling Transport Subsidy provisions
sections.summary: Enhanced Enabling Transport Subsidy provisions announced at last year's Committee of Supply commence in July, covering those with per capita household incomes up to $4,800.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: If you have any feedback, you can relay to us and we can perhaps work that into the details.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: I just want to share it that, especially for some of our persons with disabilities, in addition to what has been announced today, earlier at the Committee of Supply last year, we announced enhanced Enabling Transport Subsidy provisions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: These provisions will commence in July this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: My understanding is there for those with per capita household incomes up to $4,800, from July onwards, they will be covered.

sections.label: Competition and Consumer Commission monitoring
sections.summary: The Competition and Consumer Commission of Singapore will continue monitoring and surveillance to ensure sufficient competition in retail, wholesale, food, energy and other commodity markets.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Our Competition and Consumer Commission of Singapore will continue to monitor and carry out surveillance in the market to ensure that the market in different areas, whether it is retail or wholesale, whether it is food or energy or any other commodity, we will make sure that there is sufficient competition.

sections.label: Foreign worker levy freeze 2016
sections.summary: Budget 2016 included a one-year freeze in foreign worker levies for the marine and process sectors due to the oil price downturn.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In Budget 2016, there was a one-year freeze in foreign worker levies for the marine and process sectors due to the oil price's downturn.

sections.label: Foreign worker levy freeze
sections.summary: Asks whether the Government will consider a temporary freeze of foreign worker levies for affected sectors, especially construction.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Will the Government consider a temporary freeze of foreign worker levies to affected sectors, especially the construction sector?

sections.label: Graduated worker levy tiering
sections.summary: States the aim of graduated tiering of worker levies is to drive productivity and value-add in construction companies, SMEs and employers of foreign workers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: What we hope to be able to achieve in our graduated tiering of the worker levies is to drive productivity and drive value-add in many of these construction companies and many of the SMEs and companies that are employing these foreign workers.

sections.label: Nuclear energy deployment possibility
sections.summary: Asks the Ministry how serious the situation is and how it expedites possible deployment of small modular reactors or nuclear energy for independence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: If I can ask the Ministry, how serious this situation is and how this situation expedites the possibility of deployment of small modular reactor or nuclear energy in the context of being independent?

sections.label: Solar power capacity targets
sections.summary: States solar targets were exceeded five years early, with two gigawatt-peak hit last year, and ambition raised to three gigawatt-peak by 2030 and four gigawatt-peak by the second half of the 2030s.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: We have exceeded our targets five years ahead of time.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: We hit the two gigawatt-peak last year, ahead of the 2030 target that we set for ourselves.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: So, now, we are going to raise the ambition to three gigawatt-peak by 2030 – 50% more – and we are hoping to drive and accelerate solar power adoption here, to double that from last year to four gigawatt-peak by the second half of the 2030s.

sections.label: Energy efficiency grants and vouchers
sections.summary: Describes a multi-pronged approach using Resource Efficiency Grant for Emissions, Energy Efficiency Grant, and climate vouchers for switching aircon appliances from three-tick to five-tick, saving about $300 yearly.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: And we are starting a multi-pronged approach, not just to domestic users that we are encouraging to conserve energy, we are also working with big businesses to get them, to incentivise them to switch, whether it is the Resource Efficiency Grant for Emissions, the Energy Efficiency Grant, to get them to take on these things.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: We are encouraging contemporaneously our domestic users to use the climate vouchers if they have not used, to switch the aircon appliances, from the three-tick to the five-tick ones, which saves them considerable amount of money every year – about $300.

sections.label: Energy trading hub and fuel reserves
sections.summary: States Singapore built its energy trading hub position over decades, maintains strategic fuel reserves due to anticipated supply disruptions, and does not control prices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: As Deputy Prime Minister and Minister Shanmugam explained, we built our position as an energy trading hub over decades, that was a long-term move.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: We maintain strategic fuel reserves precisely because we anticipated supply disruptions and we do not control prices.

sections.label: National food stockpile assurance
sections.summary: The speaker appeals for an answer on national food stockpile and assures Singaporeans that stockpiles are sufficient and need not be activated now.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
sentences.text: On assurances to households, I would like to appeal for my second question earlier on national food stockpile to please be answered.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: And on national food stockpile, I think this is important, because I just want to assure Singaporeans that we do have sufficient stockpiles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: We are constantly calibrating and assessing the current situation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Certainly, at this point in time, there is no need to activate the stockpiles.

sections.label: Food import diversification
sections.summary: Singapore has agreements with about 180 countries and regions for food imports, enabling diversification, and food imports through the Strait of Hormuz were less than 0.5%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Today, we have about 180 countries and regions that we have, among our agreements today where we import food sources, so that enables us to diversify and divert food imports when necessary.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Earlier, I also shared that the amount of food imports through the Strait of Hormuz was just less than 0.5%.

sections.label: MOE canteen stallholder utility costs
sections.summary: On the question for MOE on canteen stallholders, utility costs for them are being monitored.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: On the question for MOE on canteen stallholders, we are monitoring the utility costs for them.

sections.label: Financial assistance and fuel prices
sections.summary: Financial assistance will be provided to students who need it most, and if fuel prices stay elevated, the market ought to accommodate higher fares, requiring consumers to adjust behaviour.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: But as Acting Minister Jeffrey Siow has mentioned, we will do our part to provide financial assistance to the students who need them most.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: But more importantly, if fuel prices continue to remain elevated at this price for a long period of time, actually, the market ought to accommodate it in the form of higher fares, which then, consumers will have to adjust their behaviours, including consumption.

sections.label: HDB instalment payment plans
sections.summary: HDB considered appeals from tenants facing financial hardship or poor business conditions by granting instalment payment plans.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: HDB had also considered appeals from tenants who are facing financial hardship or poor business conditions by granting instalment payment plans.

sections.label: Clarification on disruption duration
sections.summary: The Minister is asked to clarify whether the Government plans on the basis that current disruptions are temporary or that a more permanent and volatile global environment is beginning.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: First clarification, could the Minister please clarify whether the Government is planning on the basis that the current disruptions are temporary, or are we entering into a period of structurally more permanent and more volatile global environment?

sections.label: Economic Strategy Review Committee report
sections.summary: The Economic Strategy Review Committee is finishing its work and its report will be released shortly, focusing on strengthening Singapore's economic resilience and emphasising AI.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: At the same time, we talk about the long-term strategy: what should we do?

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: We have already set up the Economic Strategy Review Committee and they are finishing their work, and the report will be released shortly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: And in that work, we focus on how we can strengthen Singapore's economic resilience, so that is not only to respond to crisis, but to respond to long-term changes in the global economic structure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: This will include our emphasis on AI, to give us that edge and that leg-up against our competitors.

sections.label: Piped natural gas from Malaysia
sections.summary: 43% of Singapore's gas comes via regional pipelines, and Singapore constantly engages Malaysia on piped natural gas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
sentences.text: Given that 43% of our gas still comes via regional pipelines, has there been a similar high profile public Ministerial level mission to Jakarta and Kuala Lumpur, to specifically secure these essential energy lifelines?

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
sentences.text: And if so, has Singapore received formal assurances that existing piped natural gas export contracts will be fully honoured, despite escalating domestic industrial demands?

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: We constantly engage our counterparts for piped natural gas, Malaysia and Singapore.

sections.label: Private sector investment in collaboration
sections.summary: Expanding collaboration and uptake depends on private sector investments, with pricing negotiations left to the business-to-business sector.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Of course, to further expand that collaboration, to further expand the uptake, I think that is also a function of the amount of private sector investments that we need to bring alongside with us, because typically, when it comes to the actual negotiation for the pricing, we typically do not get involved and we leave it to the business-to-business sector to be involved in the direct negotiation.

sections.label: Misinformation and disinformation risk
sections.summary: Misinformation and disinformation could threaten social cohesion, with narratives polarising countries in conflict and spilling over to Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Digital Development and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Having said that, I think there is another type of risk that we have to watch out for even more.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Digital Development and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: That is the risk of misinformation and disinformation that could threaten our social cohesion, when narratives are being put forward that polarise not only the countries that are directly involved in a conflict, but also have a spillover effect on Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Digital Development and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: So, with regard to what we are watching out for, yes, cyber defence, but at the same time, misinformation and disinformation that could also give rise to tensions within our society.

sections.label: Transit passage under UNCLOS
sections.summary: All nations' ships have a right of transit passage under UNCLOS, which Singapore has ratified, and Article 44 obliges strait states not to hamper transit passage.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: It is a right of all nations' ships, to traverse.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: This right is enshrined in the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS), of which Singapore is a signatory and has ratified.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Article 44 of UNCLOS imposes a direct and an unambiguous obligation on states bordering these international straits.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: And let me quote, it states "states bordering straits shall not hamper transit passage." It also goes on to state there shall be no suspension of transit passage.

sections.label: Oil flows through Malacca Straits
sections.summary: More maritime oil, crude and refined, flows through the Straits of Malacca and Singapore than through the Strait of Hormuz.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: The Member may be aware that, in fact, if you add up all the maritime oil, crude and refined, you might be surprised that actually, more flows through the Straits of Malacca and Singapore than even the Strait of Hormuz.

sections.label: Stockpile for geographical chokepoints
sections.summary: Singapore maintains a stockpile sized for single and multiple geographical chokepoints and will increase it further.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: As I said, that is why we maintain the stockpile the way we have maintained.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: We have taken it upon ourselves to make sure that we have provided contingencies for different scenarios – from single geographical chokepoints to multiple geographical chokepoints.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: And we have sized up, based on the constraints of our own land size, whether it is single geographical chokepoint to multiple geographical chokepoints, that length of time that is required.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: And as what the Coordinating Minister for National Security opened up earlier on, we are going to increase that stockpile some more.

sections.label: Legal provisions for extreme scenarios
sections.summary: Legal provisions exist and provisions have been made even for a scenario where everything happens at once.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Today, there are legal provisions that are enshrined.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: I mean, you are talking about a sort of a "Z" scenario where everything happens and there are burning platforms everywhere.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: I assure you that even at that point in time, we have made provisions.
